I found no issues. The fix does what QA round 2 (Q3) asked: both supabase fakes now build on the probes fake, which reports gitleaks as present. The pack-rows test therefore no longer depends on whether gitleaks is on the machine. I checked this directly: with gitleaks and supabase both removed from PATH, as on CI's ubuntu runners, the full package suite passes (757/757). Before the fix, that same test failed on CI with tools.gitleaks reading SKIP.

One limit remains, and nothing fails because of it today. In doctor.test.mjs, the default probes() fake still asks the real PATH for any tool other than gitleaks, through PROBES.hasTool. Supabase and git are the tools this affects. No current test reads a row that depends on that answer: the suite is green with supabase on PATH and with it hidden. A future test that declares the supabase pack, uses the default probes() and checks every row would depend on the machine again, so this could go in the backlog as a hardening item.

This commit does not clear the user's `bundle.ci` FAIL. That failure was on 06850e3a, and the fix is at d17b55c, which only clears the check once it is pushed and CI is green. The closeout phase was set back to pending, so it still has to record the CI failure and its fix.
